claim_boundary: This demonstrates re-learning savings after prior exposure to a hidden actuator inversion.
It does not demonstrate simultaneous frozen competence on both mappings, because mapping identity is not observable to SEM.
Matched-experience controls reduce the explanation that B2 is faster merely because the agent has seen more total outcomes.
The same-history branch probe does not support slow memory as the primary carrier of retention; fast-only decisions were at least as effective as full decisions on B2, while slow-only was much worse.
Interference weakens the immediate B2 advantage, but a residual savings signal remains after longer normal-mapping exposure in the tested seeds.
